entries.sanskrit:
अष्टादशे हिरण्याक्ष- धरोद्धर्तृ-वराहयोः ।

निर्विशेषं महा-युद्धं देव-क्षोभि निरूप्यते ॥

प्रतियोद्धारं श्रुत्वा महा-मनाः शयिष्यस इति यद् उक्तं तद् विगणय्य अगणयित्वा । यतो दुर्मदः ॥१॥
word_for_word: of Hiraṇyākṣa and the Boar who lifted the earth
entries.literal_english: In the eighteenth chapter the great battle between Hiraṇyākṣa and the Boar who lifted the earth is described as agitating the gods. Hearing that his opponent had said, ‘You will lie down,’ the proud demon disregarded the statement.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: aṣṭādaśe hiraṇyākṣa- dharoddhartṛ-varāhayoḥ | nirviśeṣaṃ mahā-yuddhaṃ deva-kṣobhi nirūpyate || pratiyoddhāraṃ śrutvā mahā-manāḥ śayiṣyasa iti yad uktaṃ tad vigaṇayya agaṇayitvā | yato durmadaḥ ||1|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : vigaṇayya viśeṣeṇa gaṇayitvā sammatya ||1| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : asurasya varāhasyāpy ukti-pratyukty-anantaram | aṣṭādaśe gadā-yuddhaṃ brahma-bhītidam ucyate || pratiyoddhāraṃ śrutvā mahā-manāḥ sotsāha-cittaḥ śayiṣyase iti praśāntaye \[bhā|pu| 3.17.31\] iti yad uktaṃ tat khalu sva-vadhasyāsambhavatva-niścayāt vigaṇayya agaṇayitvā tam ahaṃ kva prāpsyāmīty anviṣyan daivāt puro dṛṣṭān nāradāt pṛṣṭāt harer gatiṃ gamanaṃ viditvā rasātalaṃ garbhodam eva praviveśa ||1|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: अभितो जयतीत्य् अभिजित् तं श्री-हरिम् । प्रकर्षेणोर्ध्वं नीयमानावनिर् येन । अग्र-दंष्ट्रया दंष्ट्राग्रेण स्व-रुचो हिरण्याक्ष-तेजांस्य् अरुण-श्रिया युक्तं यत्, तेन अक्ष्णा नेत्रेण मुष्णन्तं तिरस्-कुर्वन्तम् । अहो चित्रं वन-गोचरो मृगो वारि-चरो वराहः ॥२॥
word_for_word: called Abhijit because he conquers on every side
by whom the earth was lifted upward with force
by an eye joined with reddish luster
entries.literal_english: He saw Śrī Hari, called Abhijit because He conquers on every side, lifting the earth upward with His foremost tusk and eclipsing Hiraṇyākṣa’s splendor with an eye of reddish luster. How wondrous: a forest-ranging animal and water-ranging boar!
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: abhito jayatīty abhijit taṃ śrī-harim | prakarṣeṇordhvaṃ nīyamānāvanir yena | agra-daṃṣṭrayā daṃṣṭrāgreṇa sva-ruco hiraṇyākṣa-tejāṃsy aruṇa-śriyā yuktaṃ yat, tena akṣṇā netreṇa muṣṇantaṃ tiras-kurvantam | aho citraṃ vana-gocaro mṛgo vāri-caro varāhaḥ ||2|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : aruṇa-śriyeti akṣṇaḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ puṃvat tvaṃ ca bhāṣita-puṃskatvāt ||2|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : pūrvokte varāha-carite yuddha-līlā viśeṣato na vivṛteti tāṃ vivaritum āha---dadarśety-ādi | abhito jayatīty abhijit taṃ, abhijin-nakṣatrādhidaivataṃ vā | prakarṣeṇordhvaṃ nīyamānāvanir yena | agra-daṃṣṭrayā daṃṣṭrāgreṇa sva-ruco hiraṇyākṣa-tejāṃsy aruṇa-śriyā yuktaṃ yat tena akṣṇā netreṇa muṣṇantaṃ tiras-kurvantam | aho citraṃ vana-gocaro mṛgo vāri-caro varāhaḥ ||2|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: एह्य् आगच्छ । रसौकसां पाताल-वासिनां नोऽस्माकं सम्अर्पिता, अन्यथा पातालावतरणम् अस्या न घटत इति भावः । हिरण्याक्षेणाधिक्षेपार्थं प्रयुक्तापि भारती वस्तुतो भगवन्तं स्तौति । तथा हि---वन-गोचरो जले शयानः श्री-नारायणः स एव योगिभिर् मृग्यते, दुष्टान् वा हन्तुं मृगयत इति मृगः । अज्ञ नास्ति ज्ञो यस्मात् सर्व-ज्ञेत्य् अर्थः । सुरा अधमा यस्मात्, हे सुरोत्तम ! ममेक्षमाणस्यापि सतो माम् अनादृत्यापि त्वम् अनया सह वर्तमानो नोऽस्मदीयं स्वस्ति समस्तं मङ्गलं राज्यं यास्यसि प्राप्स्यसि नात्र सन्देहः । तथाप्य् अस्मत्-कृपया विमुञ्च इत्य् अर्थः । आसादिता लीलया स्वीकृता सूकराकृतिर् येन ॥३॥
word_for_word: of us who dwell in Pātāla
the one without ignorance, the omniscient
the lowest among gods / O best of gods
you will attain all welfare and the kingdom
entries.literal_english: ‘Come!’ Although spoken by Hiraṇyākṣa as an insult, this speech actually praises Bhagavān: the forest animal lying in water is Śrī Nārāyaṇa, sought by yogīs and taking a boar form. He will attain our welfare and kingdom; there is no doubt of it.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: ehy āgaccha | rasaukasāṃ pātāla-vāsināṃ no’smākaṃ samarpitā, anyathā pātālāvataraṇam asyā na ghaṭata iti bhāvaḥ | hiraṇyākṣeṇādhikṣepārthaṃ prayuktāpi bhāratī vastuto bhagavantaṃ stauti | tathā hi---vana-gocaro jale śayānaḥ śrī-nārāyaṇaḥ sa eva yogibhir mṛgyate, duṣṭān vā hantuṃ mṛgayata iti mṛgaḥ | ajña nāsti jño yasmāt sarva-jñety arthaḥ | surā adhamā yasmāt, he surottama ! mamekṣamāṇasyāpi sato mām anādṛtyāpi tvam anayā saha vartamāno no’smadīyaṃ svasti samastaṃ maṅgalaṃ rājyaṃ yāsyasi prāpsyasi nātra sandehaḥ | tathāpy asmat-kṛpayā vimuñca ity arthaḥ | āsāditā līlayā svīkṛtā sūkarākṛtir yena ||3|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : daitya-bhāvasyābhāsa-mātratvam eva vyarthena tadīya-vākyena bodhayati---āheti tribhiḥ | rasaukasām iti samprati tu vijite svarga evānayor vāsaḥ sampanna iti gamyate | rasāyā api pṛthvī-vivaratvān na svasti ity atra anaci ca \[pā| 8.4.47\] iti, vā śari \[pā| 8.3.36\] iti ca sa-kāra-dvaya-siddher vyākhyā-dvayam ||3|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : ehy āgaccha | rasaukasāṃ pātāla-vāsināṃ no’smākaṃ samarpitā, anyathā pātālāvataraṇam asyā na ghaṭata iti bhāvaḥ | hiraṇyākṣeṇādhikṣepārthaṃ prayuktāpi bhāratī vastuto bhagavantaṃ stauti | tathā hi---vana-gocaro jale śayānaḥ śrī-nārāyaṇaḥ sa eva yogibhir mṛgyate, duṣṭān vā hantuṃ mṛgayata iti mṛgaḥ | ajña nāsti jño yasmāt sarva-jñety arthaḥ | surā adhamā yasmāt, he surottama ! mamekṣamāṇasyāpi sato mām anādṛtyāpi tvam anayā saha vartamāno no’smadīyaṃ svasti samastaṃ maṅgalaṃ rājyaṃ yāsyasi prāpsyasi na atra sandehaḥ | tathāpy asmat-kṛpayā vimuñca ity arthaḥ | āsāditā līlayā svīkṛtā sūkarākṛtir yena ||3|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: अभवाय नाशाय भृतः पुष्टः । वस्तुतस् तु मोक्षाय भृतो धृत आश्रित इत्य् अर्थः । यो भवान् परोक्षेण चौर्येण जयतीति तथा । वस्तुतस् तु दूरत एव स्थित्वा जयतीति । संस्थाप्य हत्वा । वस्तुतस् तु योग-माया-रूपम् अचिन्त्यं बलं यस्य । अल्पं पौरुषं यस्मात् । तं त्वां सम्यक् स्थापयित्वा । भक्त्या हृदि स्थिरी-कृत्येत्य् अर्थः । हे मूढ-प्र, मूढान् प्राति आप्याययतीति तथा । प्रा पूर्ताव् इति धातुः । सुहृदां शुचः संसार-दुःखानि मृजे नाशयामि । यतस् त्वं स्मर्तुर् बान्धवान् अपि मोचयसीति भावः ।
word_for_word: making firm in the heart through devotion
I wipe away the grief of friends
you free the relatives of one who remembers you
entries.literal_english: The Lord is nourished for the destruction of the demons, or in truth is supported for liberation. He conquers indirectly, establishes and kills through the inconceivable power of yoga-māyā, and, when fixed in the heart through devotion, removes the grief of His friends and frees the relatives of one who remembers Him.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: abhavāya nāśāya bhṛtaḥ puṣṭaḥ | vastutas tu mokṣāya bhṛto dhṛta āśrita ity arthaḥ | yo bhavān parokṣeṇa cauryeṇa jayatīti tathā | vastutas tu dūrata eva sthitvā jayatīti | saṃsthāpya hatvā | vastutas tu yoga-māyā-rūpam acintyaṃ balaṃ yasya | alpaṃ pauruṣaṃ yasmāt | taṃ tvāṃ samyak sthāpayitvā | bhaktyā hṛdi sthirī-kṛtyety arthaḥ | he mūḍha-pra, mūḍhān prāti āpyāyayatīti tathā | prā pūrtāv iti dhātuḥ | suhṛdāṃ śucaḥ saṃsāra-duḥkhāni mṛje nāśayāmi | yatas tvaṃ smartur bāndhavān api mocayasīti bhāvaḥ | ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : vāstavārthe mūḍhān bhakti-vivaśān pratīti tathā-vidhaḥ ||4|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : sapatnair devair no’smākam abhavāya nāśāya tvaṃ bhūtaḥ kiṃ pālitaḥ yo māyayaiva hanti, ataḥ parokṣaṃ jayati, na tu sākṣāt taṃ tvāṃ yogamāyaiva, na tu daihikaṃ balaṃ yasya taṃ saṃsthāpya hatvā suhṛdāṃ śucaḥ śokāśrūṇi pramṛjāmi | pakṣe, abhavāya mokṣāya bhṛtaḥ dhṛtaḥ āśrita ity arthaḥ | kintu, māyayā kṛpayā asurān api yo hanti svakartṛka-hananena teṣām api sad-gatiṃ karoti | ata eva kṛpādhikyād eva parokṣo’pi sarveṣāṃ pratyakṣībhūto’pi jayasi devatāntarebhyo’lpa-sādhanenaiva pratyakṣībhūtebhyo’pi bahutara-sādhanair apy asākṣādbhūtas tvaṃ tebhyaḥ sarvebhya utkarṣeṇa vartasa ity arthaḥ | yogamāyā-rūpam acintyaṃ balaṃ yasya taṃ, alpa-pauruṣaṃ puruṣasya mahat-sraṣṭuḥ karma pauruṣaṃ viśva-sṛṣṭyādi tad api alpam ananurūpaṃ yasya taṃ tvāṃ samyak sthāpayitvā sva-hṛdaya-mandire bhaktyā sthirīkṛtyety arthaḥ | he mūḍha-pramūḍhān prāti sva-bhakti-dānenāpyayatīti tathā, prā pūrtau, suhṛdaḥ śucaḥ saṃsāra-duḥkhāni mṛje nāśayāmi yatas tvaṃ smartur bāndhavān api mocayasīti bhāvaḥ ||4|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: अस्मद् भुज-च्युतयापि गदया अशीर्णं शीर्षं यस्य तथा-भूते त्वयि सुखं स्थिते सति ये तुभ्यम् अधुना बलिं हरन्ति नवीना भक्ताः, ये च पूर्वे भक्ता ऋषयो देवाश् च, ते सर्वे स्वयम् एवोद्यमं विनैवामूला न भविष्यन्ति, किन्तु दृढ-मूल एव भविष्यन्तीत्य् अर्थः ॥५॥
word_for_word: even by the mace hurled from our arm
while you remain safe in that condition
ये तुभ्यम् अधुना बलिं हरन्ति नवीना भक्ताः
the new devotees who now bring offerings to you
ये च पूर्वे भक्ता ऋषयो देवाश् च
and the former devotees, sages and gods
ते सर्वे स्वयम् एवोद्यमं विनैवामूला न भविष्यन्ति
they will not become rootless, even without their own effort
rather, they will be firmly rooted; that is the meaning
entries.literal_english: If you remain unharmed, your head unbroken even by the mace hurled from our arm, then both the new devotees now bringing offerings to you and the former devotees—the sages and gods—will not become rootless. They will be firmly rooted without needing to exert themselves. That is the meaning.

transliteration: asmad bhuja-cyutayāpi gadayā aśīrṇaṃ śīrṣaṃ yasya tathā-bhūte tvayi sukhaṃ sthite sati ye tubhyam adhunā baliṃ haranti navīnā bhaktāḥ, ye ca pūrve bhaktā ṛṣayo devāś ca, te sarve svayam evodyamaṃ vinaivāmūlā na bhaviṣyanti, kintu dṛḍha-mūla eva bhaviṣyantīty arthaḥ ||5||

entries.sanskrit: स हरिर् अरेर् दुरुक्तान्य् एव तोमराः शस्त्र-विशेषास् तैस् तुद्यमानो व्यथ्यमानो दंष्ट्राग्र-गतां पृथ्वीं भीताम् आलक्ष्य तोदं दुरुक्त-व्यथां मृषन् सहमान एव निर्गतः । करेणुर् हस्तिनी । वस्तुतस् त्व् अरि-दुरुक्त-तोमरैर् निमित्त-भूतैस् तुद्यमानः । यथाश्रुतार्थ-ग्राहिणां ब्रह्मादीनां व्यथां दृष्ट्वा अनुकम्पया पीड्यमान इत्य् अर्थः । तोदं मृषन्न् इत्य् अस्याप्य् अयम् एवार्थः ॥६॥
word_for_word: the enemy’s harsh words were spears
seeing the frightened earth on the tip of His tusk
entries.literal_english: That Hari, pierced by the demon’s harsh words as by spears, saw the earth frightened on the tip of His tusk. Bearing the pain, He came forth like a female elephant; in the deeper sense, He was moved by compassion for Brahmā and the others who understood the words literally.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: sa harir arer duruktāny eva tomarāḥ śastra-viśeṣās tais tudyamāno vyathyamāno daṃṣṭrāgra-gatāṃ pṛthvīṃ bhītām ālakṣya todaṃ durukta-vyathāṃ mṛṣan sahamāna eva nirgataḥ | kareṇur hastinī | vastutas tv ari-durukta-tomarair nimitta-bhūtais tudyamānaḥ | yathāśrutārtha-grāhiṇāṃ brahmādīnāṃ vyathāṃ dṛṣṭvā anukampayā pīḍyamāna ity arthaḥ | todaṃ mṛṣann ity asyāpy ayam evārthaḥ ||6|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : sa tudyamāneti | atra vāstavārthena tayor nigūḍha-bhakta-bhāvatvaṃ spaṣṭam evāṅgīkṛtam ||6|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : sa harir arer asurasya durukti-tomarais tudyamānaḥ | pakṣe, ari-duruktito’marair eva nimitta-bhūtais tudyamānaḥ yathā-śrutārtha-grāhiṇāṃ brahmādīnāṃ vyathāṃ dṛṣṭvā anukampayā pīḍyamāna ity arthaḥ | todaṃ pākṣika-durukta-vyathāṃ mṛṣan | pākṣika-sūkta-sukha-prāptyā sahamāna ity arthaḥ | ata eva grāheṇa āhataḥ ahataś ca kareṇur hastinī ||6|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: सलिलान् निर्गच्छन्तम् अनुगतः सन् । हिरण्य-वत् कपिशाः केशा यस्य दैत्यस्य । झषो मकरः । करालास् तुङ्गा दंष्ट्रा यस्य । अशनि-वन्-निःस्वनो यस्य । निर्लज्जानाम् असतां किं विगर्हितम् अस्ति । निन्दा-भयाभावात् पलायनम् अपि न निन्दितम् इत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, लोकोपकाराय भुवम् उद्धरतोऽनुद्रवणम् अनुचितं मन्वानो दैतय् आत्मानम् एवाधिक्षिपति । गत-ह्रियां स्वार्थैक-पराणाम् असताम् अस्माकं किं विगर्हित-गणनास्ति, अपि तु नास्त्य् एव । धिग् अस्मान् इत्य् अब्रवीद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
word_for_word: following him as he emerged from the waters
what is blameworthy for the shameless wicked?
entries.literal_english: Following him as he emerged from the waters, the demon’s hair was tawny like gold, his tusks high and terrible, and his roar like thunder. The commentator asks what can be blameworthy for the shameless wicked; because they fear no censure, even fleeing is not condemned.

transliteration: salilān nirgacchantam anugataḥ san | hiraṇya-vat kapiśāḥ keśā yasya daityasya | jhaṣo makaraḥ | karālās tuṅgā daṃṣṭrā yasya | aśani-van-niḥsvano yasya | nirlajjānām asatāṃ kiṃ vigarhitam asti | nindā-bhayābhāvāt palāyanam api na ninditam ity arthaḥ | yad vā, lokopakārāya bhuvam uddharato’nudravaṇam anucitaṃ manvāno daitay ātmānam evādhikṣipati | gata-hriyāṃ svārthaika-parāṇām asatām asmākaṃ kiṃ vigarhita-gaṇanāsti, api tu nāsty eva | dhig asmān ity abravīd ity arthaḥ ||7|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : tam iti | atra vastutaḥ kaimutikenaiva[^83] śrī-varāha-devasya hiraṇyākṣasya ca taj-jñānād ubhayasyāpi vāstavārthasya stutāv eva paryavasānaṃ gamyate ||7|| [^83]: kautukenaiva iti ṅa| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : taṃ bhagavantam anudruto’nudhāvan, gata-hriyāṃ nirlajjānām asatām avīrāṇāṃ kiṃ vigarhitam, api tu naiva nindā | pratiyoddhāraṃ dṛṣṭvā palāyanaṃ nāyuktam ity arthaḥ | pakṣe, gatā prāptā hrīr yais teṣāṃ kṛpālūnāṃ vigarhitaṃ, api tu kṛpālutvād daṃṣṭrāśrita-bhū-rakṣaṇārthaṃ kiñcit palāyanam api na ninditam ity arthaḥ | yad vā, lokopakārāya bhuvam uddharato bhagavato’nudravaṇam anucitaṃ manvāno daitya ātmānam evādhikṣipati gata-hriyāṃ svārthaika-parāṇām asatām asmākaṃ kiṃ vigarhita-gaṇanāsti, api tu nāsty eva dhig asmān ity abravīd ity arthaḥ ||7|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: स भगवान् विश्व-सृजाभिष्टुतो विबुधैश् च प्रसूनैर् आपूर्यमाणः । पाठान्तरे विश्व-सृजां प्रसूनैर् विबुधैर् अभिष्टुत इति । सलिलस्योदस्ताद् उपरि व्यवहार-गोचरे देशे गां पृथ्वीं विन्यस्य तस्यां स्व-सत्त्वम् आधार-शक्तिं निहितवान् । अरेस् तस्य पश्यत एव ॥८॥
word_for_word: that Lord, praised by the creator
being showered with flowers by the gods
पाठान्तरे विश्व-सृजां प्रसूनैर् विबुधैर् अभिष्टुत इति
in another reading, “praised by the creator’s flowers and by the gods”
placing the Earth in a habitable region
He placed His own supporting potency in her
entries.literal_english: The Lord was praised by the creator, and the gods showered Him with flowers. He placed the Earth in an inhabitable place above the waters and placed His own supporting potency within her, as that enemy watched.

transliteration: sa bhagavān viśva-sṛjābhiṣṭuto vibudhaiś ca prasūnair āpūryamāṇaḥ | pāṭhāntare viśva-sṛjāṃ prasūnair vibudhair abhiṣṭuta iti | salilasyodastād upari vyavahāra-gocare deśe gāṃ pṛthvīṃ vinyasya tasyāṃ sva-sattvam ādhāra-śaktiṃ nihitavān | ares tasya paśyata eva ||8||

entries.sanskrit: परा पराक् पृष्ठतोऽनुषक्तं लग्नम् । तपनीयोपकल्पं सुवर्णाभरणम् । काञ्चन-मयश् चित्रो दंशः कवचं यस्य, तं दैत्यम् । प्रचण्ड-मन्युत्वम् अधिक्षेपादिकं चानुकरण-मात्रं, दैत्य-वाक्य-भीतानां देवानां भय-निवृत्तये । वस्तुतस् तेन तथानुक्तत्वेन कोपादि-हेत्व्-अभावात् ॥९॥
word_for_word: because it was not actually spoken that way
because there was no real cause for anger
entries.literal_english: The armor was attached behind and resembled a golden ornament. His fierce anger and insulting speech were only an imitation, intended to remove the gods’ fear; in truth there was no real cause for anger.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: parā parāk pṛṣṭhato’nuṣaktaṃ lagnam | tapanīyopakalpaṃ suvarṇābharaṇam | kāñcana-mayaś citro daṃśaḥ kavacaṃ yasya, taṃ daityam | pracaṇḍa-manyutvam adhikṣepādikaṃ cānukaraṇa-mātraṃ, daitya-vākya-bhītānāṃ devānāṃ bhaya-nivṛttaye | vastutas tena tathānuktatvena kopādi-hetv-abhāvāt ||9|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : parānuṣakteti | atrāpi tadvat | agrimādhyāye karālā \[bhā|pu| 3.19.8\] ity ādāv api | tathāpi saptama-skandhe yac chrī-yudhiṣṭhireṇa tad-durukti-nindanaṃ śrī-nāradena ca bhagavatas tad-aspṛśyatayā siddhāntitaṃ, tad aupādhikānukaraṇa-mātram avalambyeti jñeyam ||9|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : parā pṛṣṭhato anuṣaktaṃ lagnaṃ tapanīyopakalpaṃ svarṇālaṅkāraṃ daṃśaṃ kavacaṃ duruktais tad-antaṃ na tu sūktair iti bhāvaḥ | ata eva durukta-śravaṇena pracaṇḍa-manyuḥ, sūkta-śravaṇasya prativacanam avaśyam apekṣata ity ato bhagavad-vākye’pi dvitīyo’rtho vyākhyāyate ||9|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: ग्राम-सिंहान् शुनः । प्रतिमुक्तस्य बद्धस्य । विकत्थनं श्लोघाम् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: of one released and of one bound
entries.literal_english: The words compare worldly heroes to village lions, dogs. ‘Released’ and ‘bound’ are explained according to the context; vikatthana means boasting or self-praise.

transliteration: grāma-siṃhān śunaḥ | pratimuktasya baddhasya | vikatthanaṃ śloghām ||10|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : satyam ity-ādi śrī-bhagavad-vākyāni ca kevalopādhi-dṛṣṭyā tāni copahāsa-parāṇy api vāstavārtham api vahanti | tatra vana-gocaratvam ekānta-vāsatvaṃ jñeyam | tathāpi kṛpayā yuṣmad-vidhān grāmya-viṣayāsakta-śreṣṭhān mṛgaye mṛgayāmahe mocayitum anveṣayāmaḥ | nanv avinītān asmān kathaṃ kṛpayasi ? tathāha---na mṛtyu-pāśair iti ||10|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : grāma-siṃhān śunaḥ | vīrā asmad-vidhāḥ pratimuktasya baddhasya, pakṣe vana-gocarāḥ vana-sthais tyakta-viṣaya-bhoair bhaktair eva dṛśyās tad api kṛpayaiva grāma-siṃhān grāma-sthā viṣayāsaktās tan-mukhān api mṛgaye sva-padaṃ dātum anveṣayāmi | nanv ātma-ślāghino durvinītān kathaṃ kṛpayasīti tatrāha---vīrāḥ asmad-vidhā dayā-vīrās tava vikatthanaṃ doṣaṃ na gṛhṇanti | ata eva tava kathaṃ-bhūtasya mṛtyu-pāśaiḥ pratimuktasya atiśayena tyaktasya asamad-anukampita-jane mṛtyor anadhikārāt | he abhadra ! na vidyate bhadraṃ yasmāt ||10|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: न्यास-हरा निक्षेप-हराः । द्राविताः पलायनं कारिताः । अथाप्य् असमर्था अपि तिष्ठामः । तत् किम् ? यतः स्थेयं स्थातव्यम् एवास्माभिः । तत् किम् ? इत्य् अत आह---क्व यामः ? गन्तव्य-देशाभावात् ॥११॥
word_for_word: even though we are powerless, we still remain
where can we go? There is no place to go
entries.literal_english: “Nyāsa-hara” means a thief of deposited property. “Drāvita” means driven to flee. Though unable, we still stand our ground. Why? Because we must remain. Why? “Where can we go?” There is nowhere to go.

transliteration: nyāsa-harā nikṣepa-harāḥ | drāvitāḥ palāyanaṃ kāritāḥ | athāpy asamarthā api tiṣṭhāmaḥ | tat kim ? yataḥ stheyaṃ sthātavyam evāsmābhiḥ | tat kim ? ity ata āha---kva yāmaḥ ? gantavya-deśābhāvāt ||11||

entries.sanskrit: पद्-रथानां पदातीनां ये यूथ-पास् तेषाम् अधिपः । मुख्य इत्य् अर्थः । अस्वस्तये पराभवार्थम् आशु घटस्व यतस्व । अनूहो निर्वितर्कः । यो नातिपिपर्ति न पूरयति पालयति वा असाव् असभ्यः सभायाम् अनर्हः ॥१२॥
word_for_word: ये यूथ-पास् तेषाम् अधिपः मुख्य इत्य् अर्थः
their group leader is their chief; that is the meaning
for our defeat; quickly make an effort
यो नातिपिपर्ति न पूरयति पालयति वा
one who does not fulfill, complete, or keep [his word]
such a one is unfit for an assembly
entries.literal_english: “Pad-rathas” means foot soldiers; their leader is their commander. “Aśvastaye” means for defeat; strive quickly. “Anūha” means without deliberation. One who does not fulfill or keep his word is “asabhyā,” unfit for an assembly.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: pad-rathānāṃ padātīnāṃ ye yūtha-pās teṣām adhipaḥ | mukhya ity arthaḥ | asvastaye parābhavārtham āśu ghaṭasva yatasva | anūho nirvitarkaḥ | yo nātipiparti na pūrayati pālayati vā asāv asabhyaḥ sabhāyām anarhaḥ ||12||

entries.sanskrit: सोऽधिक्षिप्तः सत्यं वयम् इति श्लोकेन । रुषा प्रलब्ध उपहसितश् च एते वयम् इति द्वाभ्याम् । क्रीडां कार्यमाणोऽहि-राट् महा-सर्प इव ॥१३॥
word_for_word: he was rebuked by the verse beginning “We are indeed”
रुषा प्रलब्ध उपहसितश् च एते वयम् इति द्वाभ्याम्
mocked in anger by the two verses beginning “These are we”
like a king of serpents being made to perform
entries.literal_english: He was rebuked by the verse beginning “We are indeed...” and mocked in anger by the two verses beginning “These are we...” He was like a king of serpents being made to perform.

entries.sanskrit: मन्युना प्रचलितानि क्षुभितानीन्द्रियाणि यस्य ॥१४॥
word_for_word: whose senses were moved and agitated by anger
entries.literal_english: “Whose senses were agitated” means whose senses were shaken by anger.

entries.literal_english: “Antaka” means death.

entries.sanskrit: सौम्य विदुर । तां गदाम् अप्राप्ताम् एवाहनत् ॥१७॥
word_for_word: he struck that mace before it had reached him
entries.literal_english: “O gentle Vidura.” He struck that mace before it reached him.

entries.sanskrit: हर्यक्षो हिरण्याक्षः ॥१८॥
entries.literal_english: “Haryakṣa” means Hiraṇyākṣa.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: haryakṣo hiraṇyākṣaḥ ||18||

entries.sanskrit: स्पृधोः स्पर्धमानयोः । तिग्माभ्यां गदाभ्याम् आहतान्य् अङ्गानि, तयोः क्षताद् आस्रवतीति क्षतास्रवं रुधिरं, तस्य घ्राणम् अवघ्राणं, तेन विवृद्धो मन्युर् ययोः । विचित्रान् मार्गान् गदा-युद्ध-भ्रमण-भेदान् । इला गौः, तस्यां निमित्त-भूतायां शुष्मिणोः मत्तयोर् वृषभयोः । प्रस्तुतेऽपि इला पृथ्वी, तद्-अर्थम् । वृषभौ हि खलु बहूनि दिनानि सङ्ग्रथितोत्तुङ्ग-शृङ्ग-संहर्ष-विदीर्णाङ्ग-गलद्-रुधिरौ परस्परोपमर्द-व्यग्रोग्र-संरम्भौ चमत्कारित-गज-यूथपौ युध्यमानौ तिष्ठत इति प्रसिद्धम् ॥१९॥
word_for_word: of the two rivals, competing with each other
whose limbs were struck by sharp maces
blood flowing from the wounds of the two
whose anger was increased by it
varied movements and patterns of mace fighting
as the example, of two enraged bulls
in the present context, “ilā” also means the Earth
वृषभौ हि खलु बहूनि दिनानि सङ्ग्रथितोत्तुङ्ग-शृङ्ग-संहर्ष-विदीर्णाङ्ग-गलद्-रुधिरौ परस्परोपमर्द-व्यग्रोग्र-संरम्भौ चमत्कारित-गज-यूथपौ युध्यमानौ तिष्ठत इति प्रसिद्धम्
it is well known that two bulls fight on, their high horns locked for many days, bodies torn and bleeding, fiercely intent on crushing one another and astounding a herd of elephants
entries.literal_english: The two rivals are the two who compete with one another. Their limbs were struck by sharp maces; from their wounds flowed blood, whose smell increased their anger. They moved in varied patterns of mace combat. “Ila” means a cow, and as an example it refers to two enraged bulls. In this passage “Ila” also means the Earth. It is well known that two bulls, locked together for many days, their tall horns clashing, their bodies torn and blood flowing, fiercely intent on crushing each other, astonish a herd of elephants as they continue fighting.

transliteration: spṛdhoḥ spardhamānayoḥ | tigmābhyāṃ gadābhyām āhatāny aṅgāni, tayoḥ kṣatād āsravatīti kṣatāsravaṃ rudhiraṃ, tasya ghrāṇam avaghrāṇaṃ, tena vivṛddho manyur yayoḥ | vicitrān mārgān gadā-yuddha-bhramaṇa-bhedān | ilā gauḥ, tasyāṃ nimitta-bhūtāyāṃ śuṣmiṇoḥ mattayor vṛṣabhayoḥ | prastute’pi ilā pṛthvī, tad-artham | vṛṣabhau hi khalu bahūni dināni saṅgrathitottuṅga-śṛṅga-saṃharṣa-vidīrṇāṅga-galad-rudhirau parasparopamarda-vyagrogra-saṃrambhau camatkārita-gaja-yūthapau yudhyamānau tiṣṭhata iti prasiddham ||19||

entries.sanskrit: यज्ञा एवावयवा यस्य च । मह्यां मही-निमित्तं द्विषतोः एवं विधं विमर्दनं युद्धं दिदृक्षुः स्वराट् ब्रह्मा तत्रागात् ॥२०॥
word_for_word: for the sake of the earth
entries.literal_english: Brahmā, whose limbs are the sacrifices, came there desiring to see the conflict of the two enemies on behalf of the earth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: yajñā evāvayavā yasya ca | mahyāṃ mahī-nimittaṃ dviṣatoḥ evaṃ vidhaṃ vimardanaṃ yuddhaṃ didṛkṣuḥ svarāṭ brahmā tatrāgāt ||20|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : daityasyeti | māyayā kṛpayā gṛhītatvaṃ prapañcaṃ pratyānītatvam ||20|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : māyayā śaktyā gṛhītā sva-svāmitvenāṅgīkṛtā vārāhī tanur yasya tasya māyā-bhartur varāhasyety arthaḥ | māyayā kṛpayā gṛhītatvaṃ prapañcaṃ pratyānītatvam iti sandarbhaḥ | svarāṭ brahmā ||20|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: आगत्य च नारायणम् आह---किं कृत्वा । दैत्यं विलक्ष्य । कथं भूतम् । आसन्नं प्राप्तं शौण्डीरं शौर्यं मदो वा येन । अपेतं साध्वसं यस्मात् । कृतः प्रतीकारो येन । अहार्योऽप्रतिकार्यो विक्रमो यस्य । सहस्रणीः सहस्राणाम् ऋषि-सहस्राणां नेता ॥२१॥
word_for_word: by whom a countermeasure had been made
entries.literal_english: Having come, Brahmā addressed Nārāyaṇa after seeing the demon, whose pride in valor was free from fear and whose prowess was irresistible. Sahasraṇī means the leader of thousands of sages.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: āgatya ca nārāyaṇam āha---kiṃ kṛtvā | daityaṃ vilakṣya | kathaṃ bhūtam | āsannaṃ prāptaṃ śauṇḍīraṃ śauryaṃ mado vā yena | apetaṃ sādhvasaṃ yasmāt | kṛtaḥ pratīkāro yena | ahāryo’pratikāryo vikramo yasya | sahasraṇīḥ sahasrāṇām ṛṣi-sahasrāṇāṃ netā ||21|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : eṣa iti yugmakam | ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : āsannaṃ prāptaṃ śauṇḍīraṃ śauryaṃ mado vā yena tam | ṛṣi-sahasrāṇāṃ netā sahasraṇīḥ brahmā ||21|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: हे देव ! तेऽङ्घ्रि-मूलं प्राप्तानां देवादीनाम् । एषोऽसुरः ॥२२॥ आगस्-कृद् वृथैवापराधारोपकः । तत् परिहाराय प्रवृत्तौ भय-कृत् । भीतं ज्ञात्वा दुष्कृद् अर्थ-प्राणादि-हर्ता । अस्मत्तो राद्धो लब्धो वरो येन । अन्वेषन् प्रतिरथम् अवलोकयन् । अप्रतिरथः प्रतिपक्ष-शून्यः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: among those such as the gods who have reached the root of Your feet
“āgas-kṛt” means one who falsely accuses others of offenses
when they try to redress that, he causes fear
knowing them to be afraid, he does harm, taking wealth, life, and the like
he is one who obtained a boon from us
entries.literal_english: “O Lord, this demon is among those who have reached the root of Your feet, such as the gods. He falsely accuses others of offenses; when they try to redress them, he causes fear. Knowing them to be frightened, he commits harm and takes their wealth, lives, and the like. He has received a boon from us. “Anveṣan” means looking for an opponent; “apratiratha” means having no rival.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: he deva ! te’ṅghri-mūlaṃ prāptānāṃ devādīnām | eṣo’suraḥ ||22|| āgas-kṛd vṛthaivāparādhāropakaḥ | tat parihārāya pravṛttau bhaya-kṛt | bhītaṃ jñātvā duṣkṛd artha-prāṇādi-hartā | asmatto rāddho labdho varo yena | anveṣan pratiratham avalokayan | apratirathaḥ pratipakṣa-śūnyaḥ ||23||

entries.sanskrit: यद् यस्माद् एवं-भूतोऽयं तस्माद् एनं माक्रीड माक्रीडय । हे देव ! यथोत्थितं क्षुभितम् आशी-विषं सर्पं वालः पुच्छा-कर्षणादिना क्रीडयति, तद्वत् ॥२४॥
word_for_word: a child plays by pulling its tail
entries.literal_english: Because he is like an arisen and agitated venomous snake, do not play with him, O Lord. The comparison is to a child who plays by pulling a snake’s tail.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: yad yasmād evaṃ-bhūto’yaṃ tasmād enaṃ mākrīḍa mākrīḍaya | he deva ! yathotthitaṃ kṣubhitam āśī-viṣaṃ sarpaṃ vālaḥ pucchā-karṣaṇādinā krīḍayati, tadvat ||24|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : mainam ity-ādi śrī-brahmaṇo vākyam | tādṛśa-bhagavad-yuddha-līlāveśa-mayena prema-viśeṣeṇaiśvarya-jñaṇa-saṅkocāt | ṭīkāyāṃ yad yasmāt iti vyākhyānād yadāśī-viṣam ity eva pāṭhaḥ | sarvatra caiṣa eva ato yathety adhyāhāryaiva vyākhyātam ||24|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : enaṃ mā ākrīḍaya, bālavat ajña iva svayaṃ tu vijña-cūḍāmaṇir evāsīti bhāvaḥ | yad yathā āśī-viṣaṃ sarpam utthitaṃ garuḍa iti śeṣaḥ | athavā yad yasmād āśī-viṣam utthitam enaṃ manya iti śeṣaḥ ||24|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: स्वाम् आसुरीम् । हे देव ! स्वां मायाम् । अघं पाप-रूपम् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: evil in the form of sin
entries.literal_english: O Lord, manifest Your own māyā and Your demonic power at the proper time; the evil here is in the form of sin.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: svām āsurīm | he deva ! svāṃ māyām | aghaṃ pāpa-rūpam ||25|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : māyāṃ śaktim āsthāya prakaṭīkṛtya ||25|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : svāṃ velām āsurīm | he deva ! svāṃ māyāṃ tenāsura-velāyāṃ vivṛddha-balam enaṃ tvaṃ parameśvaro’pi hantuṃ naiva prabhaviṣyatīty aiśvarya-jñānavato’pi brahmaṇaḥ premnaivāniṣṭāśaṅkitvaṃ jñeyam | yathaiśvarya-jñāna-pūrṇayor api vasudeva-devakyoḥ samudvije bhavad-dhetoḥ kaṃsād aham adhīra-dhīḥ \[bhā|pu| 10.3.29\] ity-ādi-vākyam ||25|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: वेलाम् एवाह---एषेति । लोकानां छम्बट्-करी विनाश-करी । छम्बड् इत्य् अव्ययं विनाशे वर्तते ॥२६॥
entries.literal_english: This is the time that destroys the worlds; chambaṭ is an indeclinable expression used in the sense of destruction.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: velām evāha---eṣeti | lokānāṃ chambaṭ-karī vināśa-karī | chambaḍ ity avyayaṃ vināśe vartate ||26|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : eṣeti bhayena nikaṭatva-sphūrteḥ ||26|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : chadmaṭ-karī chadmaḍ ity avyayaṃ vināśa-vācakam ||26|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: अभिजिन् मध्याह्नः । स एव मौहूर्तिको योगः सन् । मुहूर्तः शुभ-दः कालः अगाद् गत-प्रायः । अतो यावन् मुहूर्त-शेषोऽस्ति तावद् एव सु-दुस्तरम् एनं निस्तर जहि ॥२७॥
word_for_word: that itself is the muhūrta interval
as long as a remnant of the muhūrta remains
cross this difficult obstacle and kill him
entries.literal_english: Abhijit is midday, and the auspicious muhūrta has nearly passed. Therefore, while a remnant of the muhūrta remains, cross this difficult obstacle and kill the demon.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved.
transliteration: abhijin madhyāhnaḥ | sa eva mauhūrtiko yogaḥ san | muhūrtaḥ śubha-daḥ kālaḥ agād gata-prāyaḥ | ato yāvan muhūrta-śeṣo’sti tāvad eva su-dustaram enaṃ nistara jahi ||27|| ——————————————————————————————————————— jīva-gosvāmī (krama-sandarbhaḥ) : muhūrte bhavo mauhūrtiko yogaḥ kāla-viśeṣaḥ ||27|| ——————————————————————————————————————— viśvanātha-cakravartī (sārārtha-darśiṇī) : abhijit madhyāhnaḥ mauhūrtikaḥ, muhūrta eva bhavaḥ | agāt gata-prāyaḥ | ato yāvad asyāvaśiṣṭo’sti tāvad āśu dustaram enaṃ nistara jahīty arthaḥ ||27|| ———————————————————————————————————————

entries.sanskrit: त्वां मृत्युं त्वयैव शापानुग्रह-काले विहितं निर्मितम् । आसादितः प्राप्तः । शर्मणि सुखे आघेहि स्थापय ॥२८॥
word_for_word: त्वां मृत्युं त्वयैव शापानुग्रह-काले विहितं निर्मितम्
you, as death, were appointed by yourself at the time of the curse and boon
entries.literal_english: “You were appointed as death by yourself at the time of the curse and its boon.” “Āsādita” means reached. “Āghehi” means place in happiness.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: tvāṃ mṛtyuṃ tvayaiva śāpānugraha-kāle vihitaṃ nirmitam | āsāditaḥ prāptaḥ | śarmaṇi sukhe āghehi sthāpaya ||28||
